segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we have a sad lesson for you.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们为你准备了一节悲伤的课程。

segments.en: This is an intermediate level lesson about what happens when a friend or family member dies.
segments.zh: 这是关于朋友或家人去世时会发生什么的中级课程。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So, we have a lot of words that are related to all the preparations for when somebody dies and also some phrases that you can say to someone that maybe had a family member who recently passed away.
segments.zh: 因此，我们有很多词和某人去世时的各种准备工作有关，还有一些短语，是你可以对最近有家人去世的人说的。

segments.en: So before we get into all of this, we have a key word that we want to take a look at now in Vocabulary Preview.
segments.zh: 因此，在我们进入所有这些之前，我们有一个关键词，我们现在想在词汇预览中了解一下。

segments.en: Vocabulary Preview.
segments.zh: 词汇预览。

segments.en: Alright, so in Vocabulary Preview, you have that one word and it's the title of our lesson also, funeral.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以在词汇预览中，有这样一个词，它也是我们课程的标题，葬礼。

segments.en: Funeral.
segments.zh: 葬礼。

segments.en: So, funeral is an event.
segments.zh: 所以，葬礼是一个事件。

segments.en: It's something that we have.
segments.zh: 这是我们拥有的东西。

segments.en: So basically, a funeral is the time when we mourn someone who has died.
segments.zh: 所以基本上，葬礼是我们哀悼一个已经死去的人的时候。

segments.en: It's a celebration of their life.
segments.zh: 这是对他们生活的庆祝。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So it's kind of like a ceremony where you respect that person that passed away, right?
segments.zh: 所以这有点像一个仪式，你尊重那个去世的人，对吧？

segments.en: Some people will talk about the person that passed away or maybe, you know, it's time to maybe honor that person, to as you say, mourn and remember that person.
segments.zh: 有些人会谈论去世的人，或者你知道，是时候尊重那个人了，正如你所说的那样，哀悼和记住那个人。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So it's very common for people in different religions to have different traditions.
segments.zh: 因此，不同宗教的人有不同的传统是很常见的。

segments.en: In some religions, like I think in Christianity, you have a priest who will say some things that are very traditional and then say some things about the person who died.
segments.zh: 在某些宗教中，就像我在基督教中认为的那样，你有一位牧师会说一些非常传统的事情，然后说一些关于死者的事情。

segments.en: Other religions have different ceremonies.
segments.zh: 其他宗教有不同的仪式。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So today we're going to take a look at what happens in preparing a funeral.
segments.zh: 所以今天我们来看看准备葬礼会发生什么。

segments.en: Hi, Daniel.
segments.zh: 嗨，丹尼尔。

segments.en: How are you holding up?
segments.zh: 你还撑得住吗？

segments.en: I'm greatly sorry for your loss.
segments.zh: 对于你的丧亲之痛，我深表哀悼。

segments.en: Thank you.
segments.zh: 谢谢。

segments.en: I'm much better.
segments.zh: 我好多了。

segments.en: I've begun organizing everything for the funeral.
segments.zh: 我已经开始为葬礼安排一切。

segments.en: How's that going?
segments.zh: 进展怎么样？

segments.en: It's a lot harder than I imagined.
segments.zh: 这比我想象的要难得多。

segments.en: There are many things that you have to arrange.
segments.zh: 你必须安排很多事情。

segments.en: I booked a time and date with the funeral home, but I still have a lot of things to do.
segments.zh: 我预订了殡仪馆的时间和日期，但我还有很多事情要做。

segments.en: Have you brought a burial plot and a casket?
segments.zh: 墓地和棺材都准备好了吗？

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: Wendy is being cremated.
segments.zh: 温蒂要火化。

segments.en: She always talked about how she didn't want to be buried.
segments.zh: 她总是说她不想被埋葬。

segments.en: I already chose a cremation urn and we plan to spread the ashes in the ocean.
segments.zh: 我已经选择了一个火化的骨灰盒，我们计划在海洋中散布骨灰。

segments.en: I see.
segments.zh: 我明白了。

segments.en: That sounds like something she would have really liked.
segments.zh: 这听起来像是她会真正喜欢的东西。

segments.en: I'm sure the memorial service will be tasteful.
segments.zh: 我相信追悼会一定会办得庄重得体。

segments.en: You're doing a great job.
segments.zh: 你做得很好。

segments.en: Thanks.
segments.zh: 谢谢。

segments.en: It hasn't been easy, but luckily we have life insurance and Wendy left behind a detailed will that will sort out any other legal matters.
segments.zh: 这并不容易，但幸运的是，我们有人寿保险，Wendy 留下了一份详细的遗嘱，可以解决任何其他法律问题。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So a pretty interesting dialogue and I'm sure you have a lot of questions regarding some of those words and phrases that you heard.
segments.zh: 所以一个非常有趣的对话，我相信你有很多关于你听到的单词和短语的问题。

segments.en: So why don't we take a look at five key words on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不看看语言要点的五个关键词。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: So basically we have two friends in this dialogue who are discussing arrangements for a funeral and one friend is asking the other about his preparations and asks if he's bought a burial plot.
segments.zh: 所以基本上我们有两个朋友在这个对话中讨论葬礼的安排，一个朋友正在询问另一个他的准备工作，并询问他是否购买了墓地。

segments.en: Okay, burial plot.
segments.zh: 好吧，墓地。

segments.en: Now what is a burial plot and why would you buy one?
segments.zh: 现在什么是墓地，你为什么要买一个？

segments.en: Well, a plot, P-L-O-T, plot is a piece of land.
segments.zh: 好吧，一个地块，P-L-O-T，地块是一块土地。

segments.en: So you can think about this logically, a burial plot, burial to bury is a place, a space in the ground where we bury a person.
segments.zh: 所以你可以从逻辑上想，墓地，burial 来自 bury，就是地里一个埋葬人的地方、一块空间。

segments.en: Usually you buy one of these at a cemetery, right?
segments.zh: 通常你在墓地买其中之一，对吧？

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So cemeteries have some, usually a lot of land and you can pay for a piece of land.
segments.zh: 所以墓地有一些，通常是很多土地，你可以支付一块土地。

segments.en: A small portion.
segments.zh: 一小部分。

segments.en: A small portion, yeah.
segments.zh: 一小部分，是的。

segments.en: And that's a burial plot.
segments.zh: 这是一个墓地。

segments.en: Okay, good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: And well, our next word is related to what you put into this burial plot, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，我们的下一个词与你在这个墓地中投入的内容有关，对吧？

segments.en: Somebody dies and what goes into this piece of land is a casket.
segments.zh: 有人死了，进入这片土地的是一个棺材。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: And I don't know if any of you are fans of the TV show Six Feet Under, but you'll know from this TV show that there are many different kinds of caskets.
segments.zh: 而且我不知道你们中是否有人是六英尺以下的电视节目的粉丝，但你会从这个电视节目中知道有许多不同种类的棺材。

segments.en: So a casket is a box.
segments.zh: 所以棺材是一个盒子。

segments.en: You can have fancy caskets or you can have wooden caskets that are very simple, like pine.
segments.zh: 你可以有花哨的棺材，或者你可以有非常简单的木棺材，比如松木。

segments.en: And basically this is the box that the person's body will go into when they're buried.
segments.zh: 基本上这是人的尸体被埋葬时会进入的盒子。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: So that is called a casket.
segments.zh: 所以这被称为棺材。

segments.en: Well moving on, a new trend I would say in many countries and many people around the world don't want to be buried.
segments.zh: 接下来，我想说，在许多国家和世界各地，很多人都不想被埋葬，这是一种新趋势。

segments.en: So what happens?
segments.zh: 那接下来会怎么样？

segments.en: You get cremated.
segments.zh: 你被火化。

segments.en: Cremated.
segments.zh: 火化。

segments.en: So this is the option for people who are not buried.
segments.zh: 所以这是不土葬的人的一种选择。

segments.en: In some countries, China for example, I don't think you can be buried.
segments.zh: 在一些国家，例如中国，我认为你不能被埋葬。

segments.en: You have to be cremated because there's an issue of space.
segments.zh: 你必须被火化，因为有空间问题。

segments.en: And this is an option for most people where basically your friend or your loved one, their body is burned and you can collect the remains afterwards.
segments.zh: 对大多数人来说，这是一种选择，基本上就是你的朋友或你爱的人，遗体被火化，之后你可以领回骨灰。

segments.en: They're very small.
segments.zh: 它们非常小。

segments.en: They're ashes.
segments.zh: 它们就是骨灰。

segments.en: So it's like a burning process.
segments.zh: 所以这就像一个燃烧的过程。

segments.en: Okay, interesting.
segments.zh: 好，挺有意思。

segments.en: So the word is to be cremated, to get cremated.
segments.zh: 所以这个词就是 be cremated，也就是被火化。

segments.en: Yeah, his body was cremated.
segments.zh: 是的，他的身体被火化了。

segments.en: And well as you said, you take the ashes and you can put them in a cremation urn or just an urn.
segments.zh: 正如你所说，你把骨灰装进火葬骨灰盒，或者普通的骨灰盒里。

segments.en: Okay, urn.
segments.zh: 好的，骨灰盒。

segments.en: This might sound like a strange word to you.
segments.zh: 这对你来说可能听起来像是一个奇怪的词。

segments.en: But an urn is a special kind of pot, okay, or a vessel to hold things in.
segments.zh: 但是骨灰盒是一种特殊的罐子，或者说是一种用来装东西的容器。

segments.en: So for example, in this case we have a cremation urn that is a special pot, usually very beautiful.
segments.zh: 例如，在这种情况下，我们有一个火葬骨灰盒，它是一种特殊的罐子，通常非常漂亮。

segments.en: Sometimes there's a name on it with the deceased person's ashes, his or her remains.
segments.zh: 有时上面有一个名字，里面装着死者的骨灰，也就是他或她的遗体。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: So as you said, it's kind of like a vase or a pot, something very nice and small where you have the person's ashes.
segments.zh: 所以正如你所说，它有点像一个花瓶或罐子，一个非常好、很小、用来放逝者骨灰的东西。

segments.en: All right, so now we know what happened during the funeral.
segments.zh: 好吧，现在我们知道葬礼期间发生了什么。

segments.en: We know what happens, how you maybe cremate the person or you put them in a casket.
segments.zh: 我们知道会发生什么，你如何将这个人火化，或者你把他们放在棺材里。

segments.en: And well, what happens afterwards?
segments.zh: 好吧，之后会发生什么？

segments.en: Well, afterwards you have a memorial service.
segments.zh: 好吧，之后你有一个追悼会。

segments.en: Okay, so many people want to know what's the difference between a funeral and a memorial service.
segments.zh: 好吧，很多人想知道葬礼和追悼会有什么区别。

segments.en: In my mind, a funeral is very quiet and sad and you have some respectful words and you usually put the casket into the ground or have some kind of ceremony.
segments.zh: 在我看来，葬礼非常安静、悲伤，会有一些表达敬意的话，通常会把棺材埋入地下，或者举行某种仪式。

segments.en: But a memorial service is an opportunity to talk to friends and family, to eat some food, to have some drinks, to talk about the person who died.
segments.zh: 但追悼会是一个与朋友和家人交谈、吃点东西、喝点酒、谈论死者的机会。

segments.en: It's almost like the party, if that makes sense.
segments.zh: 这几乎就像派对一样，如果这有意义的话。

segments.en: Yeah, exactly.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: It's a get together of people who obviously are trying to give support to their friends or their family members who lost that person, but also to talk about that person in a good way and all the great memories they had.
segments.zh: 这是一群聚在一起的人，他们显然是想给失去那个人的朋友或家人一些支持，同时也好好聊聊那个人，以及他们拥有的所有美好回忆。

segments.en: I guess that's why it's called a memorial service because you remember and you give out your memories about that person.
segments.zh: 我想这就是它被称为追悼会的原因，因为你会怀念并分享你对那个人的回忆。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: Okay, great.
segments.zh: 好，太好了。

segments.en: So a lot of interesting words there, very specific to this topic, but obviously really important.
segments.zh: 所以那里有很多有趣的词，非常特定于这个主题，但显然真的很重要。

segments.en: So why don't we go back and listen to the dialogue again.
segments.zh: 那么我们为什么不回去再听一次对话。

segments.en: Hi Daniel, how are you holding up?
segments.zh: 嗨，丹尼尔，你好吗？

segments.en: I'm greatly sorry for your loss.
segments.zh: 对你失去亲人，我深表哀悼。

segments.en: Thank you.
segments.zh: 谢谢。

segments.en: I'm doing much better.
segments.zh: 我做得好多了。

segments.en: I've begun organizing everything for the funeral.
segments.zh: 我已经开始为葬礼安排一切。

segments.en: How's that going?
segments.zh: 进展怎么样？

segments.en: It's a lot harder than I imagined.
segments.zh: 这比我想象的要难得多。

segments.en: There are many things that you have to arrange.
segments.zh: 你必须安排很多事情。

segments.en: I booked a time and date with the funeral home, but I still have a lot of things to do.
segments.zh: 我预订了殡仪馆的时间和日期，但我还有很多事情要做。

segments.en: Have you brought a burial plot and a casket?
segments.zh: 墓地和棺材都准备好了吗？

segments.en: No, Wendy is being cremated.
segments.zh: 不，温蒂要火化。

segments.en: She always talked about how she didn't want to be buried.
segments.zh: 她总是说她不想被埋葬。

segments.en: I already chose a cremation urn and we plan to spread the ashes in the ocean.
segments.zh: 我已经选择了一个火化的骨灰盒，我们计划在海洋中散布骨灰。

segments.en: I see.
segments.zh: 我明白了。

segments.en: That sounds like something she would have really liked.
segments.zh: 这听起来像是她会真正喜欢的东西。

segments.en: I'm sure the memorial service will be tasteful.
segments.zh: 我相信追悼会一定会办得庄重得体。

segments.en: You're doing a great job.
segments.zh: 你做得很好。

segments.en: Thanks.
segments.zh: 谢谢。

segments.en: It hasn't been easy, but luckily we have life insurance and Wendy left behind a detailed will that will sort out any other legal matters.
segments.zh: 这并不容易，但幸运的是，我们有人寿保险，Wendy 留下了一份详细的遗嘱，可以解决任何其他法律问题。

segments.en: All right, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So we have a couple of phrases, four to be exact, that we want to take a look at now in Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 所以我们有几个短语，确切地说是四个，我们想看看现在流利表达。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: Okay, this first phrase is a very useful one if you're trying to ask someone about maybe how they're feeling or someone who's had some problems recently.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果你想问问某人感觉如何，或者关心一个最近遇到麻烦的人，那么第一个短语非常有用。

segments.en: You can ask them how things are going.
segments.zh: 你可以问他们事情进展如何。

segments.en: One person says to the other, hi Daniel, how are you holding up?
segments.zh: 一个人对另一个人说，嗨，丹尼尔，你好吗？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: How are you holding up?
segments.zh: 你怎么样？

segments.en: Now you know that to hold up something means to have it in your hands, but in this case you're talking about how are things going?
segments.zh: 现在你知道，举起某物意味着把它放在你的手中，但在这种情况下，你在谈论事情进展如何？

segments.en: Right, but I wouldn't say, hey, how are you holding up?
segments.zh: 对，但我不会说，嘿，你还好吗？

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: You wouldn't say that to somebody, right?
segments.zh: 你不会对某人说的，对吧？

segments.en: If normal circumstances.
segments.zh: 如果是正常情况。

segments.en: If Marco looks really happy, I won't ask him.
segments.zh: 如果马可看起来真的很开心，我不会问他。

segments.en: But if someone has passed through a very difficult period, for example, if someone dies in their family or perhaps if they've been very sick or there's some negative or difficult things that happened, you can say, how are you holding up?
segments.zh: 但是，如果有人经历了一段非常困难的时期，例如家里有人去世，或者他们病得很重，或者发生了一些糟糕、艰难的事情，你可以说，你还好吗？

segments.en: So basically means how are you dealing with this difficult situation or how are you dealing with your illness?
segments.zh: 所以基本上意味着你如何处理这种困难的情况，或者你是如何处理你的疾病的？

segments.en: How are you holding up?
segments.zh: 你怎么样？

segments.en: Or how are you holding up with your in-laws?
segments.zh: 或者你跟你的岳父母、公婆相处得怎么样？

segments.en: Right, exactly.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: How are you dealing with that difficult situation?
segments.zh: 你是如何处理这种困难的情况的？

segments.en: And then the person complemented this by saying, and this is a very good phrase, this whole sentence is very useful if you want to say something nice to a person that has recently lost someone.
segments.zh: 然后这个人接着说道——这是一个非常好的短语——如果你想对最近失去亲人的人说些安慰的话，这整句话非常有用。

segments.en: You say, I am greatly sorry for your loss.
segments.zh: 你说，对你失去亲人我深表哀悼。

segments.en: Okay, so you might have heard the word loss before, lose, loss.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以你可能以前听过 loss 这个词，lose，loss。

segments.en: Loss is a noun, it's a thing.
segments.zh: 损失是名词，它是一个东西。

segments.en: We normally say this about people who have died because you don't want to say, I'm really sorry for your dead brother.
segments.zh: 我们通常是对有人去世的人这么说，因为你不想说：我为你死去的兄弟感到难过。

segments.en: It's sad, it's very rude, too direct.
segments.zh: 很伤心，很粗鲁，太直接了。

segments.en: So in English we say, I'm greatly sorry for your loss, for this part of your life that has gone away.
segments.zh: 所以在英语中，我们说，对你失去亲人我深表哀悼，为你生命中已经逝去的这一部分。

segments.en: You can also say, I'm very sorry for your loss.
segments.zh: 你也可以说，对你失去亲人我深表哀悼。

segments.en: This is a standard phrase for funerals and memorial services.
segments.zh: 这是葬礼和追悼会的标准短语。

segments.en: So if somebody's brother died, you go up to that person and you can say, I am greatly sorry for your loss.
segments.zh: 所以如果某人的兄弟去世了，你走到那个人面前，可以说，对你失去亲人我深表哀悼。

segments.en: I am very sorry for your loss.
segments.zh: 对你失去亲人，我深表哀悼。

segments.en: That's what you say.
segments.zh: 这就是你所说的。

segments.en: And it's very respectful and it's very nice to say.
segments.zh: 它非常尊重，很高兴说。

segments.en: Yes, it's very nice.
segments.zh: 是的，非常好。

segments.en: All right, so now moving on, we've said that the person is sorry and everything, but then they were talking about the girl Wendy and that she had life insurance and that she also left behind a detailed will.
segments.zh: 好吧，那么继续，我们说过这个人表达了歉意等等，但后来他们谈到了温迪这个女孩，她有人寿保险，还留下了一份详细的遗嘱。

segments.en: Does that mean she forgot it?
segments.zh: 这是否意味着她忘记了？
